body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil. A user can get a notification email for a topic without having a `topic_users` row (for example a mention or a category/group watch where no row exists yet), and then `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the page returns a 500. Handle the nil case, e.g. `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` or `find_or_initialize_by`.

This GET changes state and does not stop at any level. Each request moves the user down one step (watching -> regular, then regular -> muted on the next hit). A second click on the email link, a page reload, or a link prefetcher/scanner in a mail client will silently mute a topic the user only meant to drop to regular. Because it is a plain GET there is also no CSRF protection, so any site can embed `` and mute topics for logged-in users. Show a confirmation and change the level with a POST/PUT, or at least make the change idempotent (set a fixed target level).

The level is written with `tu.save!`, so it skips `TopicUser.change`. That means no `notifications_reason_id`/`notifications_changed_at` update and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish, which the normal set_notifications path does. Open clients will show a stale notification state. Use `TopicUser.change(...)`.

`unsubscribe_link` is shared by every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, and it now requires an `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation. Only `UserNotifications#notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller (other mailers, plugins, existing specs that build MessageBuilder with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`) will get a missing-interpolation error or a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` in the link. Use a separate key for the per-topic line and only add it when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

The `List-Unsubscribe` header still points only at user preferences, even though a per-topic `unsubscribe_url` is now available. Also note that clients follow List-Unsubscribe automatically. If this header is switched to the new GET endpoint, it will mute topics automatically because of the side-effecting GET (see the controller comment).

The client route only loads the normal topic view JSON and never calls the unsubscribe endpoint. If a user reaches `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` through in-app (client-side) navigation, the page says "You will stop receiving notifications" but no notification level is changed. Only full page loads hit the Rails action.

The triple-stache renders the result of `I18n.t` without escaping. It is only safe while `fancyTitle` is always pre-escaped server-side and the translation strings are trusted. Consider escaping the title explicitly before interpolating it. Also, the property name is misspelled (`stopNotificiationsText`).
